clue.text: Naval writer made a martyr

indicators.note: made is read as 'made into', so the letters of the two words that follow are reworked into the writer's name

explanation.surface: A seafaring author has turned someone into a martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' asks for the letters of 'a martyr' to be rearranged. Captain Frederick Marryat was a Royal Navy officer who wrote sea novels such as Mr Midshipman Easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Marryat served as a naval captain before becoming a novelist of life at sea.

clue.text: Serpentine poet, from centre to North

parts.note: the centre of something is its middle

explanation.surface: A poet of winding verse has travelled from the middle of the country up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are simply joined in order. 'Serpentine' describes the poet's tortuous plots and verse; Thomas Middleton was a Jacobean playwright and poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Middleton was a Jacobean dramatist and poet known for twisting, intricate plots.

clue.text: Defence put up by painting on inclination

indicators.note: in a down clue the word on places the painting under the inclination

parts.note: a ramp is an inclined slope
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Defensive works were built beside a painting set on a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is an earth bank or wall raised to defend a fort.

clue.text: American reportedly with zero intelligence in fact award-winning dramatist

parts.note: a Yank is informal for an American

indicators.note: reportedly says the pieces are to be heard, so the sound is spelt in a different way

parts.note: zero is O and intelligence is WITS, together said 'oh wits'

explanation.surface: A dim American is said, in fact, to be a prize-winning playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' tells us that O plus WITS, said aloud, gives the ending spelt OWITZ. Susan Yankowitz is an American playwright who won an Obie award; 'in fact' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Yankowitz is an American playwright whose work earned an Obie award.

clue.text: Weight of Hardy NCO

definitions.meaning: ... weight is the system used for precious metals
Sergeant ... is the soldier in Thomas Hardy's Far from the Madding Crowd

explanation.surface: How heavy is the sergeant in Thomas Hardy's novel?
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is a system of weights for gold and silver, and Sergeant Francis Troy is the dashing soldier in a Hardy novel.

clue.text: Novelist usually follows old record

parts.note: an old record is an LP, and this novelist's surname is normally preceded by the initials L.P.

explanation.surface: A writer habitually comes after an old record in the listings.
explanation.walkthrough: An LP (long-playing record) is an old record format; the novelist L. P. Hartley, author of The Go-Between, is normally written with those initials before his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: L. P. Hartley was an English novelist best known for The Go-Between.

clue.text: Well brought-up, like Brian Aldiss's lad

definitions.meaning: raised with careful attention by a person, as a reared animal is
Brian Aldiss wrote the novel The ... Boy

explanation.surface: A properly raised boy, like the one in an Aldiss novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something raised by hand has been nurtured carefully, and Aldiss titled his 1970 novel The Hand-Reared Boy.

clue.text: The girl from Chicago

parts.note: the heroine of the musical and film Chicago is the murderess ... Hart

explanation.surface: A young woman from the Windy City.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicago here is the musical, not the city: its heroine is Roxie Hart.
explanation.definitionFit: Roxie Hart is the leading female character of the musical Chicago.

clue.text: Dutch exponent of the flute

parts.note: the Dutch poet J. H. ..., whose verse is likened to a flute's music

explanation.surface: A Netherlands flautist.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a musician, but it points to J. H. Leopold, the Dutch symbolist poet, whose delicate verse is the 'flute'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jan Hendrik Leopold was a Dutch poet whose lyrical verse fits the picture of a flute player.

clue.text: Positive affirmations of Irish Penelope

parts.note: the Penelope episode of Joyce's Ulysses is Molly Bloom's monologue, full of the word of assent

explanation.surface: An Irish woman named Penelope keeps agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: Penelope is the last episode of James Joyce's Ulysses, Molly Bloom's monologue, which repeats the word of assent and ends on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated words of agreement are the hallmark of Molly Bloom's closing monologue in Ulysses.

clue.text: The genius of Hubert Selby

definitions.meaning: a genius in the old sense is an attendant spirit
Hubert Selby Jr wrote the novel The ...

explanation.surface: The brilliance of the American author Hubert Selby.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius in its classical sense is a guardian spirit or daemon, and Selby's 1976 novel is titled The Demon.

clue.text: "Think how poor thou wast, how ;/ Whom a small lump of flesh could poison thus " (John Donne, Of the Progress of the Soul)

definitions.text: "Think how poor thou wast, how ;/ Whom a small lump of flesh could poison thus " (John Donne, Of the Progress of the Soul)

parts.words: "Think how poor thou wast, how ;/ Whom a small lump of flesh could poison thus " (John Donne, Of the Progress of the Soul)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: Donne's word means exposed or vulnerable to harm

explanation.surface: A line from Donne's Second Anniversary with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The gap takes the word in its old sense 'exposed to harm', which fits a soul that a small lump of flesh could poison.
explanation.definitionFit: In Donne's time the word meant liable to injury, which suits the frail soul of the poem.

clue.text: Composer of excerpt from the Iliad (Overture and Variations)

indicators.note: an excerpt is a short run taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Music drawn from a Homer-themed suite of overture and variations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excerpt from' points to letters running across 'Iliad' and 'Overture'. Anatoly Liadov was a Russian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatoly Liadov was a Russian composer of miniatures such as Baba Yaga and Kikimora.

clue.text: The —, annually created as the judges of law and equity" (Gibbon, Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire)

definitions.text: The —, annually created as the judges of law and equity" (Gibbon, Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire)

parts.words: The —, annually created as the judges of law and equity" (Gibbon, Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: the Roman magistrates elected each year to administer justice

explanation.surface: A line from Gibbon with the name of some Roman officials missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman magistrates elected yearly to preside over the courts held that title.

clue.text: A's source of building materials

parts.note: a place where clay is dug and fired is a source of building materials; it is also the title of a novel by the author at 5-across

explanation.surface: Where someone gets materials for building.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue starts 'A's', but the novel of this title is by L. P. Hartley (5-across), so the number 5 was probably misread as 'A'.
explanation.definitionFit: A field where bricks are made supplies the material for building, and Hartley's 1964 novel bears this name.

clue.text: All-Italian mass performance

definitions.meaning: a passage played by the whole orchestra together

explanation.surface: Everyone from Italy performing together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction meaning 'all' marks a passage played by the full ensemble.

clue.text: Exalted description of Liszt piece

explanation.surface: An ecstatic review of a work by Liszt.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusive and rapturous writing is described this way, as is a work like Liszt's Hungarian Rhapsodies.

clue.text: Raised its New Order, and made a mockery

indicators.note: a new order for the letters means the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regime raised its new order and was ridiculed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Order' asks for the letters of 'Raised its' to be put in a fresh order.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon something with ridicule is to make a mockery of it.

clue.text: Native Americans, like the one McMurtry landed on the moon

definitions.meaning: a Plains tribe of the American West

definitions.text: like the one McMurtry landed on the moon
definitions.meaning: Larry McMurtry wrote the novel Comanche Moon

explanation.surface: Indigenous Americans, like the astronaut McMurtry sent to the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Plains Indian people of Texas give their name to McMurtry's novel Comanche Moon.

clue.text: Zen ethics rewritten by philosopher

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters of the two words are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A thinker revises the moral teachings of Zen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' asks for the letters of 'Zen ethics' to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was the German philosopher of Thus Spoke Zarathustra.

clue.text: Distinctive nature Huxley associated with anthropoid

definitions.meaning: the fundamental quality that makes a thing what it is
Aldous Huxley's novel Ape and ... pairs this word with ape

explanation.surface: A distinctive character linked by Huxley to an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The intrinsic nature of something is its core quality, and Huxley's novel Ape and Essence pairs the word with an anthropoid.

clue.text: Renegade classical pianist whose jazz is associated with art

definitions.text: Renegade classical pianist whose jazz is associated with art

parts.words: Renegade classical pianist whose jazz is associated with art
parts.note: the jazz pianist whose first name was Art, a classical-style virtuoso who turned to jazz

explanation.surface: A rebellious classically trained pianist whose jazz is linked with fine art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting here: it is the first name of Art Tatum, the virtuoso jazz pianist whose technique classical pianists admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was a jazz pianist of classical virtuosity, so his name is joined to 'Art'.

clue.text: Old seaman (one of five) identifies Roman king

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
a quin is one of quintuplets, five born together

explanation.surface: An old sailor, one of five siblings, recognises a Roman monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identifies' joins wordplay to definition. Tarquin was the name of two early kings of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarquinius Priscus and Tarquinius Superbus were legendary kings of early Rome.

clue.text: Base knight who lost his garter

definitions.text: Base knight who lost his garter

parts.words: Base knight who lost his garter
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Henry VI Part 1 Talbot tears the Garter from a cowardly knight

explanation.surface: A dishonourable knight had his garter taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: The garter is the Order of the Garter: in Henry VI Part 1 Talbot strips it from Sir John Fastolfe for cowardice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Fastolfe is the cowardly knight degraded from the Order of the Garter in Henry VI Part 1.

clue.text: Tale with a moral, or part of a blessing

indicators.note: part of says the letters are a run taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A story with a moral, or a section of a grace before meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' points to letters running across 'of a blessing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop's stories are the classic tales ending in a moral lesson.

clue.text: "The Pawnees and the -s were neighbouring but hostile nations" (W. G. Simms, Southward Ho!)

definitions.text: "The Pawnees and the -s were neighbouring but hostile nations" (W. G. Simms, Southward Ho!)

parts.words: "The Pawnees and the -s were neighbouring but hostile nations" (W. G. Simms, Southward Ho!)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: a Plains tribe living near the Pawnee in Nebraska

explanation.surface: A line from Simms with one Plains tribe's name missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siouan Plains people of Nebraska were neighbours and rivals of the Pawnee.

clue.text: Critic despised by Voltaire, from the Société du Coffre Rond

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A critic Voltaire loathed came from a French society of the round chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to letters running across 'Coffre Rond'. Élie Fréron was a journalist and Voltaire's bitter enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Élie Fréron was the French critic whom Voltaire attacked and ridiculed.

clue.text: Toadlike old driver

definitions.meaning: driving furiously, like Mr Toad in The Wind in the Willows
an old jocular name for a coachman or driver

explanation.surface: A driver from the past resembling a toad.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical king who 'driveth furiously' gave his name to reckless drivers, which Mr Toad was.

clue.text: Masters' runners, perhaps

parts.note: John Masters wrote Nightrunners of Bengal, so its runners come from Bengal

explanation.surface: Athletes competing in a veterans' race, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masters' is not veteran athletes: it is the novelist John Masters, whose Nightrunners of Bengal makes its runners natives of Bengal.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Bengal are described this way, as are the night-runners of John Masters's novel.

clue.text: Direction taken by Saint Exupéry's mail

definitions.text: Direction taken by Saint Exupéry's mail

parts.words: Direction taken by Saint Exupéry's mail
parts.note: Saint-Exupéry's first novel is Courrier Sud, in English ... Mail

explanation.surface: Which way the French aviator's letters went.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point names Saint-Exupéry's novel Southern Mail about airmail pilots.

clue.text: Craig Thomas made such a decision

definitions.text: Craig Thomas made such a decision

parts.words: Craig Thomas made such a decision
parts.note: the thriller writer Craig Thomas wrote a novel titled with a green gem and the word decision

explanation.surface: A thriller writer reached a particular verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'decision' is a book title: Craig Thomas wrote the thriller Emerald Decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A green gemstone gives the first word of Craig Thomas's thriller Emerald Decision.

clue.text: Spirits that may have a soul of their own, thought Paracelsus

definitions.text: Spirits that may have a soul of their own, thought Paracelsus

parts.words: Spirits that may have a soul of their own, thought Paracelsus
parts.note: Paracelsus wrote that water nymphs gain a soul by marrying a human

explanation.surface: An alchemist pondered whether spirits could possess souls.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracelsus described female water elementals who could win a soul by marrying a mortal.
